Demonstrated experience in quality improvement initiatives that enhance patient outcomes.
Experience providing and/or overseeing patient care.

The University of California, Irvine is seeking qualified candidates for a full-time Clinical Associate – Medical Intensivist position providing ICU coverage to join its expanding critical care program. Clinical service will be based primarily at UCI Health – Fountain Valley, with a 1.0 FTE commitment of 168 twelve-hour shifts per year. This position offers an opportunity to become part of a dedicated, physician-led ICU service as the hospital transitions to a closed critical care model. The candidate will join a team of intensivists responsible for providing comprehensive care, leading multidisciplinary rounds, implementing evidence-based clinical practices and contribute to the development of quality improvement initiatives and the critical care medicine program.
Clinical responsibilities will involve:

Provide comprehensive care to critically ill medical patients in the ICU, including diagnosis, treatment, and management of acute and chronic respiratory failure, shock, sepsis, multi-organ failure, and other life-threatening conditions.

Perform critical care procedures (e.g., endotracheal intubation, central venous and arterial line placement, chest tube insertion, bronchoscopy, percutaneous tracheostomy, advanced ventilator management).
Lead daily multidisciplinary ICU rounds, developing and coordinating individualized patient care plans.
Consultation and Collaboration
Serve as the attending intensivist for patients admitted to the medical ICU.
Provide critical care consultation for patients on hospital wards, ED, and other units as requested.
Collaborate closely with hospitalists, emergency physicians, subspecialists, nurses, respiratory therapists, and ancillary staff to ensure high-quality patient-centered care.
Ensure evidence-based practice standards and adherence to institutional protocols for ICU management.
Engage in frequent and compassionate communication with patients’ families regarding goals of care, prognosis, and treatment options.
Participate in family meetings, advanced care planning, and end-of-life discussions when appropriate.
Quality, Safety, and System Roles
Contribute to ICU quality improvement initiatives, patient safety programs, and guideline development.
Participate in ICU administrative duties as assigned, including mortality/morbidity reviews and ICU performance improvement.
Assist in developing and updating ICU policies, procedures, and clinical pathways.
Ensure appropriate documentation, billing, and handoff of ICU patients.
Support safe transitions of care to hospital wards or outpatient settings.
Adhere to departmental policies, procedures, and objectives in compliance with all UC policies and procedures. Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with all state and federal privacy laws.
Leadership skills: ability to motivate, inspire, communicate with staff and peers to maintain a professional, team-based approach in the care of patients.
